claims.fact: Historical matched comparison is 256 fixed-input forwards: token0 one-token prefill; tokens1..255 cached; warmup0..127; measurement128..255. All four RESULT scope fields explicitly state performance, not numerical equivalence.

Original OLD AIME generate_one uses a whole-prompt model call with an all-ones attention_mask. It samples the first output from unquantized prefill cache. Only each following cached decode is followed by C128 QDQ before the next decode; prefill_quantized=False.

Matched OLD_H_C128 applies QDQ only at t>0 (255 applications); matched NEW_H_C128 applies it also at t=0 (256 applications). Identical measured indices do not repair the distinct warmup-cache lineage.

The newer prospective worker token-steps every input from an empty cache and performs H_C128 or Dual-M QDQ after every model forward, including token0. Saved current logits precede this outer QDQ and quantify the current transition driven by earlier cache; next-token effects begin on the next forward.

OLD architecture chunk fallback uses native g.cumsum(dim=-1); NEW core installs numerical().chunk_binding(...,compensated), changing exactly that scan site to FP32 Neumaier compensated scan. The recurrent helper body is not replaced by this binding.

Architecture converts q,k,v,beta,g to FP32 inside GDN and returns FP32 recurrent state; current readout casts to the original query dtype. Historical matched records observe actual state shape[1,32,128,128] FP32 for both chunk and recurrent; BF16 model parameters are shared.

The model obtains initial_state from cache.layers[layer].recurrent_states[0], and update_recurrent_state copies each new state into the persistent cache buffer. C128 then overwrites that buffer with dequantized values in place. Source data flow supports next-token QDQ consumption, but old matched records did not retain a per-token byte-consumption proof.

Hadamard patch normalizes q/k when requested, then transforms each by float32 H128/sqrt(128) immediately before both chunk and recurrent GDN core; v is unchanged. OLD calls construct H per transform; NEW formal(True) memoizes the constant H matrix by shape/dtype/device.

C128 source uses source=state.detach().float(); scale=max_K(abs(source)).clamp_min(1e-12)/127; codes=round(source/scale).clamp(-127,127); dequant=codes*scale; state.copy_(dequant.to(state.dtype)). For state[B,32,128,128], scale is[B,32,1,128] in FP32. Codes here remain floating-point temporaries; persistent state is FP32 QDQ carrier, not a packed INT8 runtime.

Visible C128/OLD cache source stores one reconstructed recurrent buffer per GDN layer, without a separate persistent unquantized state. Transient source/dequant variables are not evidence of a persistent shadow. Actual alias graph and decorated/hub-selected implementation remain a future execution gate.

NEW Observe checks each updated state finite, verifies initial-state pointer against the prior QDQ cache, and optionally checks byte SHA. OLD matched wrapper checks actual state shape/dtype and full-logit finite; it does not implement the same state-finite or QDQ pointer/byte gate. Adding such gates in a separate numerical qualification is necessary, and their overhead must not enter the historical TPS window.

A successful NEW compensated-route contract explicitly leaves old_historical_parity=FAIL_UNCHANGED and new_matched_panel_only=True. It cannot qualify restored native OLD or supply an OLD Future-KL teacher.

available_prior_policy.scan_error_rule: Each prefix k absolute error versus CPU FP64 cumulative sum <= (gamma_k(FP32)+gamma_k(FP64))*sum(abs(input[0:k])). No empirical inflation factor. Every prefix finite. Raw relative error also reported, not divided by near-zero as pass criterion.

future_minimal_preregistration_recommend.fresh_gate: Strict byte repeatability of this restored protocol required for formal deterministic scientific use; if it fails, preserve exact earliest difference and numerical magnitude, mark runtime reproducibility fail rather than relax tolerance. Mathematical correctness and repeatability are separate gates.
